title: Characterizing Functions That Are Simultaneously Even and Odd
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Can a function be both even and odd? Give a mathematical proof justifying your answer.
finalAnswer: \text{Yes: the zero function } f(x) = 0 \text{ (on any symmetric domain } D\text{) is the unique function that is both even and odd.}

steps.title: Write the Simultaneous Conditions for Evenness and Oddness
steps.explanation: Suppose a function f defined on a symmetric domain D (where -x in D whenever x in D) is both even and odd. Then f(-x) must equal both f(x) and -f(x) for every x in D.
steps.why: Definitions of even and odd functions applied simultaneously.

steps.title: Equate the Two Expressions for f(-x) and Solve for f(x)
steps.explanation: By transitivity of equality, f(x) = -f(x). Adding f(x) to both sides gives 2f(x) = 0, and dividing by 2 proves that f(x) = 0 for every x in D.
steps.why: Zero is the only real number equal to its own additive inverse.

steps.title: Verify the Converse for f(x) = 0
steps.explanation: Conversely, the constant zero function f(x) = 0 satisfies both f(-x) = f(x) and f(-x) = -f(x) everywhere on its symmetric domain (its graph, the x-axis, is symmetric about both the y-axis and the origin).
steps.why: The zero function satisfies both symmetry identities trivially.
